DATE Thursday, Aug. 6, 2026 at 4:30 p.m. ET CALL PARTICIPANTS Chief Investor Relations Officer-Salli Schwartz Chairman and Chief Executive Officer-Mick Farrell Chief Financial Officer-Aaron Bloomer TAKEAWAYS Revenue -- $1.46 billion, reflecting 9% growth year over year or 8% in constant currency. Non-GAAP EPS -- $2.95, representing 16% growth driven by sales volume and gross margin expansion. Non-GAAP Gross Margin -- 62.3%, a 90 basis point increase year over year primarily driven by manufacturing productivity and efficiency. FY 2027 Revenue Guidance -- $5.75 billion to $5.85 billion, representing 5% to 7% growth on a reported basis. FY 2027 Non-GAAP EPS Guidance -- $12.00 to $12.25, reflecting 7% to 10% growth on a reported basis. Free Cash Flow -- $1.65 billion for the full fiscal year 2026, which the company used to return over $1 billion to shareholders. Capital Returns Target -- $1.85 billion for fiscal year 2027, an increase of over 75% year over year through dividends and buybacks. Astral Provision -- $42 million, representing the total estimated cost for the global field safety corrective action. Astral Revenue Headwind -- $75 million, resulting from the decision to suspend sales of the platform throughout fiscal year 2027. MatrixCare Divestiture Impact -- $220 million in revenue and $58 million in non-GAAP operating profit in fiscal year 2026, with the sale expected to close on or around Sept. 1, 2026. Residential Care Software Revenue -- $172 million, representing 2% growth in constant currency for the quarter. Global Sleep Device Revenue -- $750 million, up 7% in constant currency, partially driven by the AirSense 11 rollout. Global Masks and Other Revenue -- $542 million, up 10% in constant currency, reflecting strong demand for fabric mask technology. R&D Expenses -- $106 million, a 22% increase primarily driven by development of next-generation devices and AI patient workflow solutions. SG&A Expenses -- $296 million, an 11% increase reflecting marketing investments and the Noctrix acquisition. Dividend Increase -- 10% increase to $0.66 per share, as announced by the Board of Directors. GLP-1 Adherence Data -- 11% higher therapy start rate for patients using both positive airway pressure and GLP-1 medications compared to those using therapy alone. Oura Partnership Performance -- 13,000 users referred to ResMed.com, with 75% of those assessed identifying as previously undiagnosed. CapEx Guidance FY27 -- $160 million to $180 million, focused on expanding and automating global manufacturing footprints. Share Repurchase Target -- $1.5 billion planned for fiscal year 2027, including a $450 million accelerated program following the MatrixCare sale. Non-GAAP Operating Margin -- 35.2%, a 10 basis point decrease year over year. Adherence Impact -- 6% higher compliance at 90 days for the AirTouch N30i fabric mask compared to its silicone equivalent. Clinician Training -- 5,000 courses completed by 55,000 unique clinicians to improve sleep health screening and diagnosis referrals. Need a quote from a Motley Fool analyst? Email [email protected] RISKS Bloomer stated, "this is a higher cost than what we've seen on a prior astral accrual that we took primarily just because it's impacting a higher population of devices out in the field," noting the $42 million provision. Bloomer noted that the company "can no longer offset inflation with productivity alone," requiring the implementation of modest price increases across the global customer base. Bloomer indicated that "ongoing macro uncertainty and inflation across electronic components and freight" continue to present headwinds to gross margin expansion. SUMMARY Management for ResMed Inc. ( RMD +0.03% ) detailed a strategic transition to focus on core Sleep and Breathing Health segments through the divestiture of the MatrixCare business and the integration of restless leg syndrome therapy via the Noctrix acquisition. The company reported that it is addressing persistent supply chain inflation through a combination of manufacturing productivity improvements and modest price adjustments while maintaining a primary focus on volume growth. Management significantly increased its capital return targets for fiscal year 2027, including an accelerated share repurchase program and a 10% dividend hike. The company is expanding its digital health ecosystem by leveraging generative AI tools and wearable technology partnerships to capture a larger portion of the undiagnosed sleep apnea population. Operational efforts in the coming year are focused on completing the field safety corrective action for the Astral platform and scaling next-generation device launches in global markets such as China. CEO Farrell noted that "awareness has been our greatest challenge and our greatest opportunity" in underpenetrated core markets, with wearables and GLP-1 medications acting as primary demand drivers. The new Gen AI powered digital sleep coach in the MyAir app has recorded more than 1.5 million inquiries, which management reported has significantly reduced traditional customer service inquiries. CEO Farrell observed that patients on GLP-1 medications are 6% more likely to have a resupply event at three years, suggesting the medications serve as a tailwind for therapy adherence. The company reported a shift in patient demographics, with Farrell noting "higher percentages of women and we're seeing high percentages of younger patients coming into the pipeline." Management confirmed that ResMed products remain exempt from Section 301 tariffs under the Nairobi Protocol, ensuring no impact from recent U.S. tariff announcements. CFO Bloomer noted that the $75 million Astral revenue headwind represents an approximately 15 cent earnings per share impact, which is already accounted for in fiscal year 2027 guidance. CEO Farrell attributed sales growth in fabric masks to being a "change in the basis of competition," with the AirTouch N30i driving 6% higher compliance than silicone versions. INDUSTRY GLOSSARY APAP : Automatic Positive Airway Pressure, a device that automatically adjusts pressure levels on a breath-by-breath basis. Bilevel PAP : A device that provides two different levels of air pressure, one for inhalation and one for exhalation, used for complex breathing disorders. CPAP : Continuous Positive Airway Pressure, the standard therapy for treating obstructive sleep apnea. GLP-1 : Glucagon-Like Peptide-1, a class of medications used for weight loss and diabetes that ResMed identifies as a tailwind for sleep apnea diagnosis. HME/DME : Home Medical Equipment or Durable Medical Equipment, the primary distribution channel for ResMed's clinical products. OSA : Obstructive Sleep Apnea, a chronic condition where breathing repeatedly stops and starts during sleep. PCBA : Printed Circuit Board Assembly, an electronic component highlighted as a supply priority for device repairs. RCS : Residential Care Software, ResMed's business segment providing out-of-hospital software solutions. RLS : Restless Leg Syndrome, a sleep disorder that ResMed is now addressing through the acquisition of Noctrix. One, continued operational excellence and innovation excellence. To support ResMed's ongoing growth and transformation. Two, active portfolio management across our product lines and our businesses, and three, leveraging our strong free cash flow to both reinvest in our business and return capital to shareholders. A key focus area this year will be ResMed's growth and transformation work. ResMed's core markets remain largely underpenetrated. For many years, awareness has been our greatest challenge and our greatest opportunity. Now as wearables and GLP-1s gain traction, appreciation of the importance of sleep health is growing. In order to leverage this awareness opportunity effectively, ResMed needs to optimize the sleep healthcare pathway. We're seeing greater sleep health awareness among consumers with more and more people tracking their sleep with wearables and non-wearable sleep technology in their bedrooms. All the while recognizing the clinical importance of good sleep health and its correlation to overall health. This increased attention needs to be met with high-quality trusted data. As an example of this, let me talk about a recent ResMed partnership. With the wearable ring-based technology company called Oura. Approximately 13,000 users have come to ResMed.com from the Oura app with thousands of them taking the ResMed sleep assessment and approximately seventy five percent of those assessed identifying as previously undiagnosed. This highlights the potential of consumer wearables to drive earlier sleep health intervention. As another example of tech companies involved with sleep health, Samsung has just announced that its Galaxy Ring is pursuing FDA clearance for its sleep apnea detection capability. Later this year. Another sleep pathway enabler are glucagon-like peptides or GLP-1s. As we've discussed before, patients on GLP-1s both initiate CPAP more and stay on CPAP therapy with a higher adherence and resupply rate. As an update to our analysis built from a claims database of many tens of millions of patients, our specifically analyzed cohort now includes more than n = 2.5 million de-identified patients. They also more than three percent more likely to have a resupply event at one year, and more than six percent more likely to have a resupply event at three years. As we've talked about before, sleep apnea risk factors include age, gender, and craniofacial anatomy. As well as weight. OSA therefore very often persists even after significant weight loss and still needs to be treated with gold standard therapy. During the sleep medical conference this June, ResMed highlighted several interesting data sets, including one showing that among newly diagnosed OSA patients, pap therapy was initiated earlier than GLP-1s. Specifically, the data showed that at ninety days, after a positive OSA diagnosis, more than forty percent of patients had started on PAP versus less than three percent starting on a GLP-1. The proportion of patients with PAP increased immediately after diagnosis, while GLP-1 initiations increased more gradually. We continue to see GLP-1 medications as a tailwind for ResMed's business. As we continue to study the OSA population patient population more broadly, we're seeing some significant demographic shifts We're seeing higher percentages of women and we're seeing high percentages of younger patients coming into the into the pipeline. Watch this space. It's an exciting opportunity.
